name: Example: Computing the Value of a Function of a Diagonal Matrix
worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and a diagonal matrix $D$ with diagonal entries $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n,$ we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072904/assets/fd9855d724ad4cac8d8f5f93aa81455aea3f0848c744b02fbafc2987054dc7d7.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡D & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(100) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{log}⁡(1) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \operatorname{log}⁡(10)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
